abstract: [European heart journal. Digital health] Digital applications have high potential in myocardial infarction management. This study aims to harmonize personal health data using a workflow driven by an Artificial Intelligence-assisted virtual assistant prototype, then reuse the data to facilitate the creation of standardized patient summaries and risk assessment. The required configurations for data documentation and curation were developed to drive the workflow execution. With consent and data transfer agreements, data of patients with myocardial infarction were extracted from multi-source medical records, structured, and ingested into the workflow. After transformation, personal health data were mapped into concrete clinical concepts connected with specific relationships defined by the reference ontology, forming source health knowledge graphs as the basic structure of personal health knowledge graphs. Then the constructed graphs were validated using Shapes Constraint Language-based constraints, triggering the human-in-the-loop process to enhance data quality. Information queries were conducted for data reuse. Thirty eight out of 45 planned patients were recruited with signed informed consent. Thirty patients finalized the study. The overall successful data ingestion rate is approximately 83%. The average data quality score is 95.45/100. Constructed personal health knowledge graphs can be reused to represent medical information as an international patient summary and evaluate individual risk of future cardiovascular events by calculating the Second Manifestations of Arterial Disease risk score. Our proposed workflow is feasible for semi-automated personal health data curation and secondary use. It provides a potential solution to enhance medical data interoperability, thereby facilitating risk assessment in cardiovascular diseases.

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Mahidol University; conditions: Metabolic Syndrome (MetS); type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 89; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Metabolic syndrome is a group of conditions that increase the risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. These conditions include abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, elevated blood glucose, high triglyceride levels, and low levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol. Dietary habits and lifestyle are important factors influencing metabolic health. Research suggests that dietary fiber and resistant starch may support metabolic health by promoting beneficial gut bacteria and the production of short-chain fatty acids, which may help regulate inflammation and metabolism. However, individual responses to different high-fiber foods may vary. This study aims to investigate the metabolic responses of adults with metabolic syndrome to high-fiber foods from different sources, including foods containing resistant starch and antioxidants. The study will also develop a machine learning model to predict individual nutritional and metabolic responses to high-fiber foods and support personalized nutrition strategies for metabolic syndrome prevention in the Thai population. The research is part of an international collaboration involving Thailand, Australia, and Indonesia to improve understanding of differences in dietary responses across individuals and populations. A total of 89 participants will be recruited in Thailand. Eligible participants will be adults aged 18-60 years, of any sex, who meet the International Diabetes Federation criteria for metabolic syndrome. abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fertoolity S.L.; conditions: Ovarian Follicle Monitoring, Controlled Ovarian Stimulation; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 66; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Monitoring ovarian follicles is an important part of fertility treatments, as it helps healthcare professionals assess how the ovaries respond to stimulation. Traditionally, follicles are measured manually using two-dimensional (2D) ultrasound, a process that can be time-consuming and may vary between operators. This study aims to evaluate the accuracy of OSIS (Online System for Image Segmentation), an artificial intelligence (AI)-based software that automatically identifies and measures ovarian follicles using three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound images. Women undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization (IVF), egg donation, or fertility preservation will participate in the study at fertility clinics in the United States and Europe. During their ovarian stimulation monitoring visits, conventional manual 2D ultrasound measurements will be compared with automated measurements obtained using OSIS. The study will also assess the consistency of measurements across different healthcare professionals, clinical settings, and ultrasound equipment, as well as the time required for each measurement method.

abstract: Brain field potentials (FPs) reflect the combined activity of multiple neural sources, challenging the accuracy of their temporal series and their spatial origin difficult to establish from waveform inspection alone. However, FP generators obtained by independent component analysis exhibit characteristic temporal patterns and unique spatial profiles that allow their identification, even during apparently irregular activity. Here, we compared feature-based machine learning (ML) and end-to-end deep learning (DL) approaches to assess how effectively this information can be extracted from short segments and whether learning directly from raw signals offers advantages over predefined signal descriptors. We analyzed irregular FP-generator activity from multiple hippocampal generators in a dataset pooled across experimenters, recording devices, and electrode types. Feature-based approaches used predefined spectral and nonlinear descriptors to construct multidimensional representations, which were classified using seven ML algorithms: bagged decision trees (BAG), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA), random forest (RF), support vector machines (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGB) and multilayer perceptron (MLP). In parallel, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer architectures learned discriminative representations directly from raw signals. Performance was evaluated using animal-independent data partitions to assess generalization to previously unseen animals. Both approaches discriminated among FP generators from short segments of irregular activity. Raw-signal models generally achieved higher classification performance than feature-based approaches, although the latter also captured substantial generator-specific information. This suggests that discriminative information extends beyond the predefined descriptors and includes temporal patterns that can be exploited through direct signal learning. Classification across animals further supports the reproducibility of generator-related information despite variability in experimental conditions and recording procedures. These findings provide a scalable quantitative approach to identifying FP generators from irregular activity, opening new possibilities for investigating electrophysiological signals across physiological and pathological conditions.
zh_abstract: 脑场电位（brain field potentials, FPs）反映多个神经源的联合活动，这使其时间序列的准确性受到挑战，并且仅通过波形检查难以确定其空间起源。然而，通过独立成分分析获得的FP发生器表现出特征性的时间模式和独特的空间分布，使得即使在不规则活动期间也能对其进行识别。在此，我们比较了基于特征的机器学习（ML）和端到端深度学习（DL）方法，以评估从短片段中提取该信息的有效性，以及直接从原始信号学习是否优于预定义信号描述符。我们分析了来自多个海马发生器的FP发生器不规则活动，所用数据集汇集了不同实验者、记录设备和电极类型的数据。基于特征的方法使用预定义的频谱和非线性描述符构建多维表示，并使用七种ML算法进行分类：袋装决策树（bagged decision trees, BAG）、轻量梯度提升机（light gradient boosting machine, LGBM）、二次判别分析（quadratic discriminant analysis, QDA）、随机森林（random forest, RF）、支持向量机（support vector machines, SVM）、极端梯度提升（extreme gradient boosting, XGB）和多层感知机（multilayer perceptron, MLP）。同时，卷积神经网络（CNNs）和Transformer架构直接从原始信号学习判别性表示。性能使用动物独立的数据划分进行评估，以评估对先前未见动物的泛化能力。两种方法都能从短片段不规则活动中区分FP发生器。原始信号模型通常获得比基于特征的方法更高的分类性能，尽管后者也捕获了大量发生器特异性信息。这表明判别性信息超出预定义描述符，并包括可通过直接信号学习加以利用的时间模式。跨动物分类进一步支持了发生器相关信息的可重复性，尽管实验条件和记录程序存在变异性。这些发现提供了一种可扩展的定量方法，用于从不规则活动中识别FP发生器，为研究生理和病理条件下的电生理信号开辟了新可能性。
